phaseHint.seed.focus.title: Gentle start
phaseHint.seed.focus.text: Keep check-ins short and regular. In the early phase, consistency and calm observation matter most.
phaseHint.seed.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.seed.calendar.text: Plan small daily checks rather than many heavy actions at once.
phaseHint.veg.focus.title: Watch growth
phaseHint.veg.focus.text: A clear watering and check routine pays off now. Open tasks should stay visible and rhythmic.
phaseHint.veg.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.veg.calendar.text: Spread training, check-ins and watering across the week so the calendar isn't overloaded on one day.
phaseHint.flower.focus.title: Flower focus
phaseHint.flower.focus.text: Use tighter check intervals, open reminders and clean log entries for anything unusual.
phaseHint.flower.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.flower.calendar.text: Use recurring tasks for flower checks and watering so the week stays plannable.
phaseHint.harvest.focus.title: Harvest window
phaseHint.harvest.focus.text: Keep final checks, notes and daily logs close together so decisions stay traceable later.
phaseHint.harvest.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.harvest.calendar.text: Deliberately block free days for control, harvest prep and log documentation.
phaseHint.dry.focus.title: Calm aftercare
phaseHint.dry.focus.text: In this phase small daily checks are often more important than many new tasks.
phaseHint.dry.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.dry.calendar.text: Use short reminders for checks and keep logs brief but regular.
phaseHint.cure.focus.title: Stay consistent
phaseHint.cure.focus.text: Recurring short check tasks help you keep the routine clean across several days.
phaseHint.cure.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.cure.calendar.text: Set fixed weekly slots for control and log entries instead of working ad hoc.
phaseHint.custom.focus.title: Own flow
phaseHint.custom.focus.text: Use templates and sets to keep your own per-plant rhythm consistent anyway.
phaseHint.custom.calendar.title: Calendar tip
phaseHint.custom.calendar.text: When the phase is individual, clear titles and clean due dates help the calendar a lot.

moon.tip.0: New moon: a rest day. Prepare the soil, don't sow.
moon.tip.1: Waxing: sow above-ground plants (lettuce, herbs, flowers).
moon.tip.2: First quarter: sow fruiting plants (tomato, bean, pepper).
moon.tip.3: Waxing: a good time for feeding and transplanting.
moon.tip.4: Full moon: harvest time! Plant vigour at its peak.
moon.tip.5: Waning: sow root crops (carrot, potato, beetroot).
moon.tip.6: Last quarter: prune, weed, control pests.
moon.tip.7: Waning: compost, work the soil, rest.
bauern.1-1.name: New Year's Day
bauern.1-1.spruch: If New Year's Day is bright and clear, it points to a fruitful year.
bauern.1-6.name: Epiphany
bauern.1-6.spruch: Twelfth Night bright and clear promises a fine wine year.
bauern.1-20.name: Fabian and Sebastian
bauern.1-20.spruch: Fabian wearing a hat of mist does the grain no harm but good.
bauern.2-2.name: Candlemas
bauern.2-2.spruch: When Candlemas brings storm and snow, spring is not far off, you know.
bauern.2-14.name: Valentine's Day
bauern.2-14.spruch: Valentine's Day with sunny skies makes a lovely autumn rise.
bauern.2-24.name: St Matthias
bauern.2-24.spruch: Matthias breaks the ice; if there is none, he makes it twice.
bauern.3-17.name: St Gertrude
bauern.3-17.spruch: Gertrude serves the gardener well, for garden work she rings the bell.
bauern.3-19.name: St Joseph
bauern.3-19.spruch: If St Joseph's day is fair, a good year will be there.
bauern.3-21.name: First Day of Spring
bauern.3-21.spruch: When violets bloom in March's light, the rosebuds glow and set alight.
bauern.4-23.name: St George
bauern.4-23.spruch: By St George's kindly grace all the trees are decked in bloom.
bauern.4-25.name: St Mark
bauern.4-25.spruch: If St Mark's day is warm and fine, plenty of grain will soon be thine.
bauern.5-1.name: May Day
bauern.5-1.spruch: Rain on Walpurgis Night has always brought a good year right.
bauern.5-11.name: Ice Saint Mamertus
bauern.5-11.spruch: Pancras, Servatius, Boniface — only then does summer take its place.
bauern.5-12.name: Ice Saint Pancras
bauern.5-12.spruch: No summer before Boniface, no frost once Sophia's passed.
bauern.5-13.name: Ice Saint Servatius
bauern.5-13.spruch: Servatius must be gone and past before you're safe from nightly frost.
bauern.5-14.name: Ice Saint Boniface
bauern.5-14.spruch: Pancras, Servatius and Boniface are three frosty rascals.
bauern.5-15.name: Cold Sophia
bauern.6-11.name: St Barnabas
bauern.6-11.spruch: St Barnabas with sunshine bright gives the grapes their honeyed light.
bauern.6-21.name: First Day of Summer
bauern.6-21.spruch: If it rains on Midsummer Day, thirty more days of rain will stay.
bauern.6-24.name: St John's Day
bauern.6-24.spruch: Plant until St John's Day — a date every gardener knows.
bauern.6-27.name: Seven Sleepers Day
bauern.6-27.spruch: The weather on Seven Sleepers Day may well for seven weeks stay.
bauern.7-2.name: Visitation of Mary
bauern.7-2.spruch: However the weather on the Visitation falls, it holds for forty days.
bauern.7-15.name: Start of the Dog Days
bauern.7-15.spruch: Dog days bright and clear show a good year is near.
bauern.7-20.name: St Margaret
bauern.7-20.spruch: If rain on Margaret's day should fall, it plagues the nuts, one and all.
bauern.8-10.name: St Lawrence
bauern.8-10.spruch: Lawrence with his fiery breath fills the farmer's cask and skin.
bauern.8-15.name: Assumption of Mary
bauern.8-15.spruch: At the Assumption of Mary the fruit is glad to turn red.
bauern.8-24.name: St Bartholomew
bauern.8-24.spruch: As St Bartholomew behaves, so the whole autumn stays.
bauern.9-1.name: St Giles
bauern.9-1.spruch: As September begins, so it holds until the end.
bauern.9-8.name: Nativity of Mary
bauern.9-8.spruch: On the Nativity of Mary the swallows fly away.
bauern.9-22.name: First Day of Autumn
bauern.9-22.spruch: If the migrant birds still linger past Bartholomew, we read a mild winter through.
bauern.9-29.name: Michaelmas
bauern.9-29.spruch: When St Michael draws near, the last leaves fall down sheer.
bauern.10-4.name: St Francis of Assisi
bauern.10-4.spruch: If St Francis brings a lovely day, unsettled weather may follow the way.
bauern.10-16.name: St Gall
bauern.10-16.spruch: St Gall leaves no cow at the fence and drives them into the barn.
bauern.10-28.name: Simon and Jude
bauern.10-28.spruch: Simon and Jude, the two, call the winter work to do.
bauern.11-1.name: All Saints' Day
bauern.11-1.spruch: All Saints' clear and bright, winter waits upon the threshold tonight.
bauern.11-2.name: All Souls' Day
bauern.11-2.spruch: November often enters with frost, yet it need not stay that cold for long.
bauern.11-11.name: St Martin's Day
bauern.11-11.spruch: St Martin comes by ancient rite with geese and bonfires burning bright.
bauern.11-25.name: St Catherine
bauern.11-25.spruch: Catherine's snow brings trees and seedlings woe.
bauern.12-4.name: St Barbara
bauern.12-4.spruch: If Barbara walks in green, the Christ Child comes in white.
bauern.12-21.name: First Day of Winter
bauern.12-21.spruch: If St Thomas' night is long, no need to fear for spring's own song.
bauern.12-25.name: Christmas
bauern.12-25.spruch: Christmas in snow, Easter in clover.
bauern.12-31.name: New Year's Eve
bauern.12-31.spruch: New Year's Eve windy and warm makes the farmer poor and forlorn.
bauern.monthWisdom.1: January: time for planning and ordering seeds. Prune fruit trees.
bauern.monthWisdom.2: February: start plants indoors. Prepare beds if the soil allows.
bauern.monthWisdom.3: March: direct sow early vegetables. Prune roses and shrubs.
bauern.monthWisdom.4: April: main sowing season! But beware of late frosts.
bauern.monthWisdom.5: May: after the Ice Saints everything goes outdoors. Don't forget to mulch.
bauern.monthWisdom.6: June: water, feed, harvest. St John's Day = last planting date for many vegetables.
bauern.monthWisdom.7: July: harvest in full swing. Start second sowings for autumn.
bauern.monthWisdom.8: August: last harvest of the summer fruit. Prepare the autumn sowing.
bauern.monthWisdom.9: September: harvest apples and pears. Sow green manure.
bauern.monthWisdom.10: October: finish the harvest. Get beds ready for winter.
bauern.monthWisdom.11: November: compost the leaves. Put winter protection in place.
bauern.monthWisdom.12: December: the garden rests. Care for your tools. Plan next year.
